industrial organic-acid product; native ecological function in U. maydis remains NR in the defining pathway study.

EasB is HR-PKS; EasD acyl-CoA ligase and EasC acyltransferase mediate transfer of the polyketide side chain to EasA; targeted deletions support all three.

Emericellamide A has reported antibacterial activity; native ecological function in A. nidulans is NR in the defining pathway work.
Putative polyketide synthase and central scaffold candidate in cluster 39; locus-to-product association is strong but enzyme chemistry was not directly reconstituted.
Putative O-methyltransferase and cytochrome P450 provide plausible tailoring functions; assignments remain annotation-level.
veA is required for normal cluster-39 expression; transcripts are enriched in sclerotia and are strongly reduced in ΔveA.
RNA-seq/RT-qPCR comparison of wild type and ΔveA plus chemical analysis of sclerotial extracts linked cluster 39 to aflavarin; no purified-enzyme kinetic values reported.
Sclerotial-associated metabolite; specific ecological/virulence function for aflavarin was not established in the defining study.
Iterative fungal PKS associated with fujikurin scaffold production; products of the PKS19 cluster were isolated and structurally characterized.
MIBiG lists additional locus genes including a toxD-like protein, but direct gene-by-gene chemical roles are not established in the defining product-isolation study.

Fujikurins A–D were isolated and assigned by NMR and high-resolution mass spectrometry; no robust pathway-wide quantitative yield series is reported in the source abstract.
Native ecological or pathogenic role of fujikurins is NR in the defining structural/pathway report.

Specific native ecological or virulence role of asperipin-2a is NR in the defining study.
Nonreducing PKS with C-methyltransferase and terminal Claisen-cyclase domains, proposed to synthesize methylphloracetophenone precursor.
Adjacent cytochrome P450 proposed to oxidatively dimerize methylphloracetophenone toward usnic acid.
Both mpas and mpao transcripts were detected by RT-PCR in a lichen sample that produced usnic acid by HPLC; no artificial activation intervention was tested.
De novo genome sequencing, in-silico PKS filtering, RT-PCR and HPLC production correlation; knockout, heterologous reconstruction and purified-enzyme validation were NF in the defining study.
Usnic acid is a characteristic lichen secondary metabolite, but this record does not establish a specific ecological function causally linked to MPAS/MPAO.
CitS nrPKS builds a trimethylated unreduced pentaketide and reductively releases a keto-aldehyde; CitA serine hydrolase supports conversion of the released intermediate.
Sequential oxidative tailoring converts methyl→alcohol (CitB), alcohol→aldehyde (CitC) and aldehyde→carboxylic acid (CitD) on the route to citrinin.
Defining work used native genetics plus heterologous A. oryzae reconstruction; no single universal environmental trigger is required to establish pathway chemistry.

Citrinin is a toxic fungal polyketide/mycotoxin; native adaptive role is not resolved by the pathway reconstruction.
Tetraketide and hexaketide synthases generate the two polyketide-derived portions of the squalestatin framework; PKS disruption abolishes SQS1 production.
Acyltransferase expressed in E. coli loads acyl-CoA side chains onto the squalestatin core; broad substrate tolerance was demonstrated.
Producing versus non-producing culture states strongly gate the locus; genes mfpks1 through mfR6 show coordinated induction.
qRT-PCR showed roughly 10^2–10^5-fold higher expression across the active interval under producing conditions; heterologous/enzymatic tests resolve late acylation.
Squalestatin S1 is a potent squalene-synthase inhibitor of pharmacological interest; native ecological role is NR in the defining cluster study.
HR-PKS, hydrolase, citrate-synthase-like enzyme and methylcitrate dehydratase form the monomer-generating core; bfpks1 knockout abolishes byssochlamic acid and agnestadride A.
Two ketosteroid-isomerase-like proteins are necessary for cyclization; PEBP-like proteins bfL5/bfL9 strongly enhance cyclized-product formation.
Transcriptomics distinguishes producing versus non-producing B. fulva conditions; heterologous A. oryzae expression provides a direct bypass of native regulation.

Maleidride natural-product family; specific native ecological role for byssochlamic acid is NR in the defining biosynthetic studies.
Ten-module NRPS identified as the core leucinostatin synthetase; domain organization is consistent with the nonapeptide/peptaibol-like scaffold.

Leucinostatins contribute antifungal/oomycete antagonism against Phytophthora and are relevant to the organism's biocontrol phenotype.

Inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase homolog with dual pathway/self-resistance role; native evidence supports protection against MPA as well as contribution to cluster function.
Native cheese-ripening strain produces MPA without an artificial activation switch; gene-silencing experiments diagnose pathway dependence rather than activation.

MPA is an immunosuppressive secondary metabolite and a relevant contaminant of blue-veined cheeses; mpaF provides fungal self-resistance.

Two citrate-processing enzymes generate the maleic-anhydride-bearing precursor architecture.
Two ketosteroid-isomerase-like proteins catalyze ring formation, assisted by PEBP-like proteins.
Producing versus nonproducing transcriptional states were used for cluster discovery; pathway causality was then tested genetically and heterologously.
Native pks disruption and A. oryzae reconstruction of core, KI-like and PEBP components; quantitative titers NR in this dossier.
Maleidrides are bioactive fungal polyketides; specific ecological role of byssochlamic acid/agnestadride production in B. fulva is UNCERTAIN.
Builds the aromatic polyketide-derived precursor used for downstream prenylation and reduction.
Installs the farnesyl substituent required before the terminal NRPS-like reduction step.
Adenylation-domain-containing NRPS-like enzyme selectively accepts the farnesylated substrate and reduces the carboxylate to the aldehyde of LL-Z1272β.

Three UstYa-family proteins required for desaturation of amino-acid moieties; knockout of each establishes essential pathway function.
SAM-dependent alpha-N-methyltransferase converting phomopsin A to the N,N-dimethylated congener phomopsin E.
Historical species-level culture work found strong dependence on static culture, medium composition, pH and temperature; these measurements are not transferred as locus-strain-specific evidence.

Gene knockouts establish UstYa-family necessity. Historical P. leptostromiformis WA1515 stationary cultures produced about 75–150 mg/L phomopsin A with approximate optima pH 6 and 25 °C; no production was detected in shaken cultures. These values are retained as non-record-strain context.
Phomopsins are antimitotic mycotoxins associated with lupinosis and microtubule disruption.
Cryptic NRPS-associated locus activated by serial replacement of native promoters with a regulatable promoter; activation yields fellutamide B.
Cluster-encoded proteasome-subunit homolog; deletion during pathway activation demonstrates a self-resistance function against internally produced fellutamide B.
Native cluster resisted earlier expression attempts; serial promoter exchange was required to force access and reveal the pathway product.
Serial promoter replacements, metabolite detection/structure assignment, inpE deletion and pathway activation; exact production titer NR.
Fellutamide B is a proteasome inhibitor; inpE provides pathway-linked producer self-resistance.
Highly reducing fungal PKS generates the reduced polyketide precursor that feeds alpha-pyrone polyene assembly.
Cluster enzymes convert the PKS-derived precursor through successive tailoring steps; two intermediates isolated during heterologous reconstruction constrain pathway order.
Cluster genes were expressed heterologously under controlled promoters in A. nidulans; a native pathway-specific activation switch in the source strain is NR.
Stepwise heterologous expression in A. nidulans, metabolite profiling and isolation of two pathway intermediates; exact native titers NR.
Citreoviridin is a mycotoxin and F1-ATPase beta-subunit inhibitor that disrupts mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation.
Pro1 forms the protoilludene sesquiterpene scaffold from FPP; ArmB supplies the orsellinic-acid-derived polyketide component used in melleolide assembly.

The core neighbourhood encodes multiple oxidative tailoring enzymes. ArmH1–ArmH5 are actively transcribed extracluster FAD-dependent halogenases with overlapping ability to monochlorinate free melleolide substrates.
A dedicated native pathway-specific activation switch was NR in the defining study; expression analysis demonstrated active transcription of multiple halogenase paralogs.
Cluster analysis, expression profiling and functional/biochemical testing of ArmH halogenases support pathway assignment; a record-strain production titer was NR.
Melleolides are bioactive Armillaria natural products; the native ecological role of the BGC and the specific contribution of halogenation in situ remain NR.
Do not interpret chlorinated/brominated product labels as evidence that halogenase genes reside inside BGC0001401; the experimentally characterized ArmH enzymes are extracluster.
TpcC is the non-reducing PKS/atrochrysone-carboxylic-acid synthase; TpcB releases the PKS product. Deleting tpc-cluster core genes eliminates trypacidin.
TpcK/TpcL and methyltransferase/oxidoreductase steps elaborate the scaffold. Incomplete TpcK catalysis generates endocrocin as a shunt; ΔtpcK raises endocrocin nearly tenfold.
Production is conidial/developmental and LaeA/BrlA-sensitive. A single-nucleotide insertion in the pathway PKS explains loss of trypacidin in a nonproducer, and CRISPR repair restores production.
Targeted deletions, HPLC metabolite profiling and CRISPR/Cas9 repair establish causality; ΔtpcK gives an approximately 10-fold endocrocin increase.
Trypacidin is conidia-associated and antiphagocytic; it is also toxic to pulmonary/bronchial epithelial cells. These host-interaction effects are distinct from the endocrocin shunt phenotype.
The tpc and enc clusters both make endocrocin, but only the tpc pathway is required for trypacidin; shared endocrocin output must not be interpreted as duplicate trypacidin causality.
SorA/Pks13 is a highly reducing PKS and SorB a non-reducing PKS; both are required to generate sorbicillin/dihydrosorbicillin pathway intermediates.

SorC is a FAD-dependent monooxygenase producing (dihydro)sorbicillinol; SorD is an oxidoreductase leading to oxosorbicillinol. SorR1 activates transcription, while SorR2 controls sorR1; SorT is an MFS transporter.
Classical strain improvement mutated/silenced pks13; repairing the mutation restored production. Sorbicillinoids themselves stimulate pathway transcription, providing metabolite autoinduction.
pks13 repair, targeted gene deletions, regulator overexpression and metabolite profiling establish the pathway; exact atlas-normalized native titer is NR.
Sorbicillinoids have reported antiviral, anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial activities; their native ecological function in Wisconsin 54-1255 is NR.

Penicillium chrysogenum in the defining papers is the historical name used for the Wisconsin lineage now represented in the canonical source as P. rubens; this is nomenclatural provenance, not evidence from another strain.
CazM is the non-reducing PKS and CazF the highly reducing PKS; CazF acts both sequentially and convergently with CazM-derived intermediates to build the azaphilone scaffold.
CazE acyltransferase partners with CazF in reconstitution. Post-PKS redox enzymes including CazL and CazP show substrate promiscuity and expand chlorinated/nonchlorinated chaetoviridin diversity.

A dedicated native pathway-specific transcriptional activation switch was NR in the defining mechanistic work; pathway access was resolved primarily by gene inactivation and biochemical reconstitution.
Targeted caz-gene deletions, LC-MS and in-vitro reconstitution establish pathway order; ΔcazF and ΔcazM abolish the principal azaphilone products. Native titers were NR in atlas-compatible units.
Chaetoviridins/chaetomugilins are bioactive azaphilones; a specific native ecological function for this C. globosum locus is NR.
MIBiG names selected products, whereas the caz cluster produces a broader family; product-family chemistry should not be collapsed to a single terminal metabolite.

The cluster contains hybrid PKS-NRPS AFLA_066840 as the principal scaffold-forming megasynthase. Cluster-level causality is strong, while not every enzyme-to-step assignment was directly purified and reconstructed in the defining study.
AFLA_066900/LepE is a Zn(II)2Cys6 transcription factor: lepE inactivation down-regulates nine predicted cluster genes and overexpression up-regulates eight, functionally delineating the pathway.
LepE overexpression activates the otherwise weakly accessed cluster, yielding orange-red hyphae and detectable leporin B plus the dehydroxy precursor leporin C.
Transcription-factor inactivation/overexpression, high-resolution MS and structural analysis support pathway access; OE::lepE reduces conidia and sclerotia. A standardized production titer was NR.
Leporin B forms a distinctive trimeric iron complex with antiinsectan/antifeedant properties; forced production also disrupts normal developmental output.
Cluster activation and product assignment are direct; individual tailoring reactions should not be promoted to direct biochemical evidence unless separately tested.
Pks27/AFLA_082150 is required for asparasone A and related sclerotial anthraquinones; Δpks27 produces greyish-yellow rather than dark brown sclerotia.

VeA acts upstream as a developmental/global regulator: veA mutation strongly down-regulates pks27. Exact downstream enzyme-to-anthraquinone tailoring assignments remain incompletely resolved in the defining work.
The pathway is sclerotium-specific and VeA-dependent; conidial pigmentation is unaffected by pks27 loss, separating this programme from canonical conidial melanization.

pks27 inactivation, TLC/MS and comparative metabolomics identify four wild-type-specific anthraquinones including asparasone A; mutant sclerotia are significantly less resistant to insects, UV and heat. Exact normalized effect sizes are NR here.
Asparasone-family pigments protect A. flavus sclerotia from biotic predation and abiotic UV/heat stress.
The protective phenotype is directly associated with pks27-derived anthraquinone pigmentation, but the contribution of each individual congener is not separately resolved.
UcsA is the PKS-NRPS assembly line and UcsL its trans-enoyl reductase partner; the NRPS module incorporates (2S,3S)-3-methylproline derived from L-isoleucine.
UcsH functions in trans-decalin-forming cyclization; UcsG supports methylproline supply, while UcsK/UcsF and other redox enzymes drive oxidation and furopyrrolizidine maturation.
Constitutive overexpression of the cluster regulator UcsR activated the silent/low-access pathway in the thermophilic host and yielded UCS1025A at approximately 200 mg/L.
UcsR activation, ΔucsA loss-of-production, isotope/feeding logic and biochemical genetics resolve the pathway; activated strain MT18 produced ~200 mg/L UCS1025A.
UCS1025A is a strong telomerase-inhibitory natural product; the native ecological function of this pathway in T. thermophilus is NR.

The original UCS1025A-producing strain Acremonium sp. KY4917 aided pathway discovery, but the functional activation/engineering evidence encoded here comes from the thermophilic host; these organism contexts are kept separate.
Mac-cluster genetics identify MacA-dependent pathway chemistry; macR overexpression was used to increase access and ΔmacA abolishes the relevant product profile.
MacJ is a membrane-bound type-II terpene cyclase that protonates the terminal olefin of acyclic meroterpenoid substrates and triggers late-stage cyclization; it shows useful substrate promiscuity.
Experimental macR overexpression was used to activate/enhance the pathway for genetic analysis; this is an engineered access condition rather than a demonstrated native ecological switch.
HPLC of wild type, macR-overexpression, ΔmacA and ΔmacJ strains plus yeast-microsome/in-vitro MacJ assays establish late cyclization. Standardized native titer was NR.
Macrophorins are bioactive isoprenoid epoxycyclohexenones; a specific native ecological function of the retired record is NR.
Do not merge retired BGC0001450 automatically with later active macrophorin records; the later mechanistic paper is used to interpret pathway architecture while retaining accession-level provenance.
The pathway’s unusual megasynthase is an iterative PKS linked to a noncanonical condensation-domain module; the PKS builds a reduced long-chain polyketide that is handed to the C-domain chemistry.

The truncated C domain is a bona fide condensation catalyst rather than a vestigial remnant: it recognizes 5-aminopentanoic acid and catalyzes amidation/release to generate wortmanamide-family products.
The pathway was accessed through genome-mining-guided experimental characterization; a dedicated native pathway-specific transcriptional switch was NR in the defining study.
Genome mining, structural characterization and direct functional analysis of the unusual C domain establish substrate selection and condensation chemistry. A record-strain production titer was NR.
Wortmanamides resemble long-chain N-acyl-amide signaling lipids structurally, but a native receptor-mediated signaling role in T. wortmannii has not been demonstrated; ecological function is NR.

The primary paper discusses a wortmanamide family, whereas the historical MIBiG record names wortmanamide singular. Family-level chemistry is preserved without inflating the retired record to products not explicitly assigned there.
AstA is the pathway terpene cyclase. AstB and AstC are cytochrome P450 monooxygenases that sequentially oxidize the AstA-derived scaffold to aspterric acid.
AstD is not a tailoring enzyme: it is a pathway-linked, aspterric-acid-resistant dihydroxy-acid dehydratase that supplies self-resistance to the metabolite’s molecular target.
The pathway was reconstructed under engineered expression in Saccharomyces cerevisiae; a native pathway-specific activation switch in A. terreus was NR in the defining study.

AstA+AstB produce an oxidized intermediate, and AstA–AstC reconstitution in yeast yields aspterric acid at about 20 mg/L. Target assays show sub-micromolar inhibition of sensitive plant DHAD, while AstD confers resistance.
Aspterric acid is a herbicidal natural product targeting dihydroxy-acid dehydratase in branched-chain amino-acid biosynthesis; AstD protects the producing pathway from that same target mechanism.

The functional four-gene programme is strongly resolved, but the database display, canonical seed and ~17-kb experimentally described neighbourhood do not coincide exactly; completeness is therefore not inferred beyond MIBiG’s unknown designation.
FFUJ_10353 is the evidence gene associated with alpha-acorenol; knockout and engineered production were used to identify sesquiterpene-synthase products.
NR
Engineered production optimization was used; native pathway-specific activation was NR.
Gene knockout, genetic engineering, isolation and spectroscopic structure elucidation; alpha-acorenol titer NR in accessible defining abstract.
NR
The broader current display is not treated as a demonstrated multi-gene pathway; completeness remains unknown.
cu-pks-4 is a transcribed iterative type I nonreducing PKS with SAT, KS, AT, PT, tandem ACP and TE architecture; pathway chemistry was inferred rather than functionally reconstituted.
Predicted neighboring FAD-binding monooxygenase, PKS-like KR-DH protein, halogenase and O-methyltransferase form a proposed isocoumarin-tailoring set based mainly on homology.
cu-pks-4 transcription was detected in lichen material; no pathway-specific activation switch was demonstrated.

Degenerate-PCR discovery, cDNA transcription test, genome annotation and homology analysis. No matching pathway metabolite was detected; defining authors stated functional expression was needed for final confirmation.
NR
MIBiG labels 6-hydroxymellein, but the defining study did not experimentally demonstrate production by this locus; causal product attribution remains UNCERTAIN.

Ten functional genes adrA and adrC-adrK were individually silenced; each silencing construct significantly reduced andrastin A, supporting cluster-wide pathway membership. adrB is a residual pseudogene relative to the homologous Penicillium pathway.
AdrC is an MFS transporter required for normal production, but silencing did not support a simple secretion-only role; remaining Adr proteins constitute biosynthetic and tailoring functions.
Native pathway-specific activator NR in the defining study; the native producing strain was interrogated by targeted RNA silencing.
RNA-mediated silencing of all ten functional adr genes, metabolite and transcript analyses; andrastin-A reductions were significant at P<0.05 in replicated experiments.
NR
Completeness remains unknown and not every Adr enzyme-to-step assignment has direct biochemical reconstitution; genetic pathway membership and enzyme chemistry are graded separately.

atnA encodes a six-module NRPS with terminal reductase; ΔatnA abolishes aspercryptins. atnF/atnM encode dedicated FAS components; ΔatnF abolishes production and is chemically rescued by octanoic plus dodecanoic acids.

atnN is a cluster transcription factor; overexpression approximately doubled aspercryptin A1. The 14-gene program also encodes aminotransferases, P450/oxidoreductase and transport/resistance functions.
Partial knockdown of histone deacetylase RpdA activated the locus and increased a family of 15 aspercryptins by up to approximately 100-fold.

Chromatin perturbation, gene deletion, transcription-factor overexpression, precursor feeding/rescue and LC-MS/NMR. Key quantitative anchors: up to ~100-fold RpdA-dependent induction; ~2-fold aspercryptin A1 increase with atnN overexpression.
NR
Current MIBiG display is broader than the seed evidence interval and completeness is unknown; untested tailoring assignments remain annotation-level.
asaC encodes the NRPS-like core biosynthetic enzyme; ΔasaC eliminates aspergillic acid and its pathway precursors, directly anchoring scaffold formation.

Targeted oxidative-enzyme knockouts resolve later steps: a P450-deficient mutant accumulates deoxyaspergillic acid, while disruption of desaturase/hydroxylase functions blocks hydroxyaspergillic-acid formation. Hydroxamate chemistry supports ferriaspergillin formation by iron binding.
A dedicated native pathway activation switch was NR in the defining study; the native producing strain was interrogated through targeted gene deletion.

Seven predicted pathway genes were knocked out and analyzed by metabolite profiling; pathway mutants also showed impaired growth and reduced aflatoxin B1/cyclopiazonic-acid accumulation during maize-associated assays.
Iron-chelating hydroxamate chemistry is directly supported; the native ecological contribution beyond iron complexation is UNCERTAIN.
Lower aflatoxin B1 and cyclopiazonic acid in pathway mutants coincided with reduced growth; these changes are not encoded as direct asa-cluster cross-regulation. MIBiG completeness remains unknown.

Direct pathway genetics were obtained in Penicillium brevicompactum: deletion of either ApmA or ApmB abolished asperphenamate, and coexpression of both genes in A. nidulans was sufficient for production. A. terreus carries homologous NRPS genes, but these experiments are not strain-specific evidence for BGC0001517.

ApmA is a reductase-terminating NRPS that generates a dipeptidyl alcohol; ApmB accepts the linear precursor and catalyzes intermolecular ester formation to assemble asperphenamate. These functions are experimentally supported in the P. brevicompactum system.
A pathway-specific activation mechanism for the exact A. terreus NIH2624 record is NR; heterologous A. nidulans coexpression demonstrates pathway sufficiency for the homologous ApmA/ApmB pair.
P. brevicompactum gene disruption, precursor feeding, stable-isotope labeling, metabolite structure analysis and A. nidulans heterologous reconstruction resolve the two-NRPS pathway.
NR

The exact MIBiG organism is A. terreus NIH2624, whereas direct ApmA/ApmB causality is from P. brevicompactum. Homologous-pathway evidence is retained as relationship evidence only; direct A. terreus locus causality remains UNCERTAIN.
AstC cyclizes FPP to drimanyl diphosphate; AstI and AstK successively dephosphorylate it to drim-8-ene-11-ol. AstA, an NRPS-like enzyme, esterifies the drimane alcohol with aryl-acid building blocks.

A 12-gene disruption series in an activated background maps additional pathway functions; purified-enzyme assays directly support the core terpene and esterification steps while other tailoring assignments retain gene-phenotype rather than complete enzyme-level resolution.

Disruption of cclA or sppA, components affecting H3K4 methylation state, derepresses astellolide production. This is a chromatin-access intervention rather than a dedicated native pathway-specific switch.
Chromatin regulator disruption, qRT-PCR/metabolomics, 12 targeted pathway-gene disruptions, purified-enzyme assays, HPLC and GC-MS/NMR were combined to map the pathway.
NR
MIBiG completeness remains unknown and the current display exceeds the seed interval; cclA/sppA are global chromatin regulators and are not encoded as dedicated astellolide genes.
The defining study identifies a highly conserved Basidiomycota nonribosomal peptide synthetase associated with biosynthesis of the trimeric hydroxamate siderophore basidioferrin.
Additional enzyme-to-step assignments beyond the experimentally characterized siderophore system are NR/UNCERTAIN and are not inferred from orthologs alone.
Iron availability is the relevant physiological context for siderophore function; a dedicated pathway-specific activation switch in this exact record was NR.
The defining study combined comparative genomics with experimental characterization of the conserved siderophore system and basidioferrin product; no unsupported quantitative yield is inferred here.
Iron acquisition via hydroxamate siderophore chemistry.
MIBiG completeness is unknown. Conservation across Basidiomycota is retained as comparative context, not as direct strain-specific evidence for every orthologous gene function.
BtcA is a bifunctional sesterterpene synthase: its C-terminal prenyltransferase generates geranylfarnesyl diphosphate and its N-terminal terpene cyclase forms the betaestacin-I scaffold.

BtcB, a cytochrome P450, catalyzes extensive oxidative conversion toward betaestacin II. BtcC (P450) and BtcD (2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase) belong to the four-gene locus, but their exact product-forming roles are less completely resolved and remain UNCERTAIN here.
The cryptic pathway was functionally accessed by heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae; a dedicated native pathway activation switch in the source fungus was NR.

Genome mining, heterologous expression of scaffold and oxidation genes, product isolation, MS/NMR and comparison with a homologous Colletotrichum orbiculare sesterterpene cluster resolved scaffold formation and oxidative diversification.
NR

Historical genus naming differs from current Neocamarosporium nomenclature. Completeness remains unknown, and BtcC/BtcD functions are not promoted beyond the experimental resolution of the defining studies.

CbCTB1 is the nonreducing PKS that anchors cercosporin perylenequinone assembly. The historical CTB1-CTB8 model captures the core locus but is insufficient to represent all experimentally required biosynthetic functions.

Functional expansion identified four additional required genes and a cercosporin facilitator/self-protection factor; late enzymes complete methylenedioxy-bridge formation. CTB2 O-methyltransferase disruption abolishes cercosporin, while CTB8 is a pathway-associated transcription factor.

Cercosporin production is light responsive and condition dependent; CTB8 contributes pathway transcriptional control. Environmental regulation is retained separately from gene-to-step biosynthetic causality.

Genome analysis, reverse genetics, targeted knockouts, metabolite profiling, plant-infection assays and phylogenomics. Δctb2 eliminates detectable cercosporin and strongly impairs disease development on sugar beet.
Photoactivated cercosporin generates reactive oxygen species and functions as a phytotoxic virulence factor; loss of pathway function reduces pathogenicity.

The historical eight-gene CTB model is incomplete as a functional description. Current MIBiG completeness nevertheless remains unknown, so the broader display boundary is not treated as a fully proven self-contained pathway.

The native C. zeina CTB cluster retains the broader cercosporin biosynthetic machinery but contains a defective CTB7 allele with indels; native cultures did not produce canonical cercosporin under the tested in-vitro conditions.

Introduction of a full-length functional CTB7 allele from C. zeae-maydis restored a red pigment chemically confirmed as cercosporin, showing that the remaining C. zeina pathway machinery is functional enough to complete the pathway when CTB7 activity is supplied.

Complemented strains produced cercosporin under nitrogen-limited medium and light. These conditions establish assay context but do not prove a native activation switch sufficient to overcome the defective CTB7 allele.
CTB-locus sequencing, identification of CTB7 indels, Agrobacterium-mediated complementation with donor CTB7, pigment assays, KOH/TLC and UPLC-QTOF confirmation of cercosporin.
C. zeina is a maize gray-leaf-spot pathogen, but the contribution of canonical cercosporin or a proposed structural variant to native in-planta disease remains UNCERTAIN.

MIBiG labels cercosporin, whereas the native strain did not produce canonical cercosporin in vitro. Donor CTB7 rescue demonstrates pathway competence, not that the native CTB7 allele is functional. A possible in-planta structural variant remains a hypothesis.

Candidate cluster contains polyketide-biosynthetic capacity consistent with the flavonoid-like scaffold; gene-to-step assignments are primarily comparative/predictive rather than native causal genetics.
Hydroxylation, O-methylation and chlorination functions were proposed from cluster content and chlorflavonin structure; direct strain-specific enzyme validation is UNCERTAIN.
NR; no pathway-specific native activation switch was demonstrated in the defining comparative-genomics study.
PacBio genome sequencing, comparative genomics, metabolite knowledge and predictive cluster analysis; no native single-gene deletion series reported for chlorflavonin.
Reported as a bioactive secondary metabolite; a specific ecological role in A. campestris is UNCERTAIN.
Do not upgrade chemistry-aware cluster assignment to gene-level causality. Current display boundary is broader than the curated evidence locus.
chry1/NRPS14 is a two-module NRPS; deletion abolished chrysogine, while overexpression enhanced production, establishing direct scaffold-pathway causality and a likely flux bottleneck.

F. graminearum candidate cluster includes chry2-chry6. Detailed individual-gene pathway assignments from P. chrysogenum are orthologous follow-up and are not treated as direct F. graminearum evidence.
Anthranilic acid and pyruvic acid are reported precursor inputs; chry1 overexpression increases production. No dedicated environmental switch was established.
Comparative NRPS analysis, chry1 deletion, overexpression and metabolite profiling; P. chrysogenum follow-up used systematic cluster-gene deletions and feeding experiments.
Chrysogine is a yellow fungal pigment; a specific F. graminearum ecological or virulence role is UNCERTAIN.
Do not transfer the complete P. chrysogenum gene-to-step map onto PH-1 as direct strain-specific evidence.
The cluster is closely related to the andrastin pathway and supplies the meroterpenoid scaffold used for citreohybridonol diversification.

Ctr-P450 is the directly demonstrated citreohybridonol synthase: coexpression with andrastin A biosynthetic genes yields citreohybridonol plus four new andrastin derivatives, showing multifunctional oxidative tailoring.
Heterologous/coexpression context demonstrates enzyme sufficiency for oxidative diversification; native environmental regulation is NR.
Cluster comparison, coexpression with andrastin biosynthetic genes, metabolite isolation and structural characterization of citreohybridonol and four derivatives.
Citreohybridonol was reported as an antifeedant agent; native ecological function in the record strain is not fully resolved.
Historical Emericella variecolor naming and current Aspergillus stellatus record naming are preserved; direct Ctr-P450 evidence is stronger than evidence for every neighboring gene.
Defining work used genome sequencing and knockout of key cluster genes to establish the cornexistin maleidride pathway; early stages resemble byssochlamic-acid/nonadride biosynthesis.
Cornexistin differs from related nonadrides by requiring fewer enzymes in the dimerization step and by removal of one maleic-anhydride moiety.
NR; study focused on pathway genetics and intermediates rather than a native activation switch.
Whole-genome sequencing, targeted gene knockouts, isolation and structural identification of pathway intermediates.
Cornexistin is a natural herbicidal maleidride; ecological function in the producing fungus is UNCERTAIN.
Do not count BGC0001557 as an independent active cluster. Organism naming/provenance differs between source row and defining paper.
The pathway combines iterative PKS and NRPS chemistry for a polyketide-peptide hybrid scaffold; heterologous reconstruction confirmed the associated cluster and proposed biosynthetic logic.

Cluster annotations include cpaN1 MFS transporter, cpaN2 transcription factor, cpaO FAD-dependent monooxygenase and additional oxidative enzymes; gene-specific native functions are not all equally validated.
Heterologous expression provided experimental access to the pathway; a native environmental activation switch is NR.
Chemical screening, bioinformatic cluster identification and heterologous expression used to confirm curvupallide/spirostaphylotrichin pathway assignment.
Specific ecological role of curvupallide-B in the producer is UNCERTAIN.
Contig-edge location prevents treating the 53-kb record as demonstrably complete; individual annotation-level genes are not automatically causal.
cycC encodes the giant cyclosporin C synthetase; its 11-module architecture matches the cyclic undecapeptide core.

The sixth adenylation-domain sequence differs from the cyclosporin A enzyme and was proposed to account for incorporation of L-threonine rather than L-alpha-aminobutyric acid; nearby genes include alanine racemase, cyclophilin, ABC transporter and regulatory candidates.
CsC was detected from fungal extracts under screening culture conditions; no dedicated pathway-specific environmental switch was established.
Differential-temperature antifungal assay, bioassay-guided fractionation, LC-MS, NMR, commercial-standard comparison, genome sequencing and cluster-synteny analysis.
CsC inhibited Cryptococcus neoformans more strongly at 37 C in the screening assay; ecological role in the producing fungus is UNCERTAIN.
A-domain specificity is a strong mechanistic hypothesis, not a direct module-swap proof. Beauveria/Amphichorda naming is preserved as taxonomy provenance.
The vidA-vidS cluster contains 19 genes, including six cytochrome P450 genes; deletion of 15 biosynthetic genes produced a dense intermediate map for furanosteroid assembly.
Pregnane side-chain cleavage requires a flavin-dependent Baeyer-Villiger monooxygenase, an esterase and a dehydrogenase, rather than a single P450 step.
NR; pathway was interrogated through genetics and metabolite-intermediate analysis rather than a defined native activation switch.
Fifteen biosynthetic-gene deletions, isolation of 14 biosynthetic intermediates, structural analysis and activity testing against PI3K.
Demethoxyviridin is a potent PI3K-inhibitory furanosteroid; producer-side ecological function is UNCERTAIN.
Functional pathway resolution is high, but current MIBiG still labels completeness unknown; flanking genes in the displayed 66.3-kb region should not automatically be assigned biosynthetic roles.
cloA encodes the decisive clavine oxidase branch enzyme. The C. africana allele accepts festuclavine and supports DHLA formation; the comparison LA-pathway CloA did not.
C. africana CloA can also oxidize agroclavine to lysergic acid in substrate-feeding assays, demonstrating broader substrate acceptance than the comparison enzyme.
Synthetic intron-free cloA expression in a festuclavine-accumulating N. fumigata mutant was required for clean heterologous testing because the genomic C. africana clone was mis-spliced.
Heterologous expression, substrate feeding, fluorescence HPLC and LC-MS; DHLA identified from an m/z 271.2 parent-ion signal matching standard behavior.
DHLA is the precursor family for pharmacologically important dihydro-ergot alkaloids; native ecological role is UNCERTAIN.
Direct biochemical evidence is strongest for cloA, not for every gene in the 27-kb record. Engineered N. fumigata production demonstrates allele function rather than native C. africana flux.
A phenalenone aromatic polyketide is converted into oxaphenalenone building blocks; DuxM, a cupin-family dioxygenase, initiates oxidative cleavage to a transient hemiketal-oxaphenalenone.
Additional redox enzymes form anhydride or dihydrocoumarin monomers. A P450 catalyzes the initial inter-monomer C-C bond; the enzyme for the second C-C bond was not identified.
Saccharomyces cerevisiae reconstruction was used to resolve pathway steps; native environmental induction is NR.
T. stipitatus gene deletions including ΔduxI/ΔduxD, LC-MS metabolite profiling, S. cerevisiae reconstruction and mechanistic redox analysis.
Duclauxins are bioactive dimeric fungal polyketides; a specific ecological role for T. stipitatus is UNCERTAIN.

The pathway spans two separated gene clusters in the defining study, so a single MIBiG display region should not be treated as the whole functional programme; the second C-C-forming enzyme remains NF.

The record is an epipolythiodioxopiperazine-like pathway related to chaetocin/verticillin families; MIBiG annotations include sulfur-handling and transport functions, but the 2018 ecological study did not systematically delete every cluster gene.
Cluster annotations include a PLP-dependent carbon-sulfur-bond lyase and an ABC transporter; individual roles are not upgraded beyond database annotation without direct E. weberi genetics.
Infection of Leucoagaricus gongylophorus by E. weberi upregulated melinacidin IV and shearinine D relative to axenic culture.
Infection-versus-axenic HPLC profiling, metabolite isolation/identification and bioactivity assays against Pseudonocardia; ant-behavior/toxicity effects were strongest for shearinine D.
Melinacidin IV functions as a virulence-associated chemical-warfare metabolite that inhibits protective Pseudonocardia during Escovopsis infection of leafcutter-ant fungus gardens.
Ecological product-role evidence is stronger than gene-by-gene pathway causality. Shearinine D is co-induced but belongs to a separate biosynthetic programme and is not merged into BGC0001585.
Fsl1 is the reducing PKS; Fsl5 supplies trans-enoyl-reductase activity, with Fsl2 implicated in product release and Fsl3 in isomerization.
Fsl4 is a P450 implicated in oxygenation/epoxidation; the terminal carboxyl-reduction step to fusarielin H remains unresolved.
Native pathway expression/production demonstrated in F. graminearum; a specific ecological induction switch was NF in the defining mechanistic sources.
Gene-function analysis plus metabolite profiling resolved the FSL pathway; fusarielins F/G/H have reported estrogenic growth effects in MCF-7 assays.
Native ecological role remains NR; fusarielin congeners have mycoestrogenic bioactivity.
Do not infer that the broad current MIBiG display defines every required pathway gene; terminal reduction remains unresolved.
A seven-enzyme cluster includes GGPP supply, bifunctional ent-copalyl-diphosphate/ent-kaurene synthase (CPS/KS), and four P450 monooxygenases.
P450-4 catalyzes three oxidations from ent-kaurene to ent-kaurenoic acid; GA4 desaturase is a 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase.
GA-cluster genes are coordinately expressed in productive F. fujikuroi states; presence of homologous clusters in related Fusarium species does not guarantee expression or GA production.
cps/ks or whole-cluster deletion abolishes diterpene production; P450-4 deletion accumulates diterpene hydrocarbons.
Fungal gibberellins are plant-growth regulators associated with the bakanae disease phenotype of rice.
The current database marks completeness unknown; classic seven-gene pathway knowledge is retained as functional programme evidence, not used to overwrite database completeness.
Gpy1/PKS13 (FFUJ_12020) is the HR-PKS; deletion abolishes gibepyrone A and complementation restores it. Its embedded C-methyltransferase installs both SAM-derived methyl groups.
Gpy2/FFUJ_12021 is an ABC transporter with minor efflux effect but represses GPY1 expression. Gibepyrones B/D arise via cluster-independent CPR-dependent P450 activity; E/F form nonenzymatically.
Vel1, Vel2 and Lae1 repress GPY expression/product formation; Sge1 positively regulates the pathway.

Stable-isotope feeding supports four acetate units plus two SAM methyls; Δgpy1 loses product; Δgpy2 increases GPY1 expression and extra-/intracellular product. Gibepyrones A/B show reported MICs of 100–200 µg/mL against tested Gram-positive bacteria/yeasts.
Native ecological role remains UNCERTAIN; gibepyrone A is also detectable in headspace and has moderate antimicrobial activity.
Oxidized congeners B/D require enzymes outside the mapped small cluster; therefore product-family execution is broader than the core BGC.
The mapped NRPS GliP/TRIVIDRAFT_78708 is the core synthetase; targeted disruption eliminates gliovirin production.
The defining study identified a 22-gene cluster with multiple predicted tailoring, transport and regulatory functions; gene-by-gene causality is less complete than NRPS causality.
Gliovirin production is part of T. virens secondary metabolism associated with biocontrol; a single pathway-specific environmental switch was NR in the defining source.
Genome mining plus targeted NRPS disruption: loss of the core NRPS abolished detectable gliovirin.
Gliovirin is anti-oomycete and contributes to the chemical arsenal underlying T. virens biological control.
Do not equate the 30-kb current display with the entire experimentally discussed 22-gene programme.
thtri5 encodes the trichodiene synthase entry step of the TRI programme; targeted deletion was used to identify the harzianum-B cluster.
Cluster organization resembles related Trichoderma trichothecene programmes, but product-specific tailoring differences are preserved rather than transferred from orthologs.
Native harzianum-B production was observed in T. hypoxylon cultures; a dedicated environmental activation trigger was NR.

Markerless gene targeting reached 89% homologous-recombination frequency in a thlig4 background; thtri5 deletion identified the TRI cluster. A separate chemistry study recovered ~50 mg harzianum B from a 1-L, 14-day culture.
Native ecological role of harzianum B remains NR in the defining genetic study.
Reason for MIBiG retirement was NF in the authoritative materials examined; retirement status itself is preserved without inventing a rationale.

HimA is the candidate PKS-NRPS; disruption abolishes normal himeic-acid biosynthesis. Labeled-precursor feeding shows the long fatty-acyl side chain is polyketide-derived and the amide substituent derives from leucine.
HimH is annotated as a dehydrogenase/trans-acting reductase partner and HimG as a dioxygenase; detailed step assignments beyond HimA are not all directly validated in the defining study.
Himeic acid A was isolated from marine-derived Aspergillus cultures; a pathway-specific induction switch was NR in the defining genetics study.

Genome sequencing, labeled-precursor feeding and HimA disruption establish the pathway. Himeic acid A inhibited E1–ubiquitin intermediate formation by 65% at 50 µM; himeic acids B/C showed little inhibition even at 100 µM.
Native ecological role is NR; biochemical activity is selective inhibition of ubiquitin-activating enzyme E1.
The contig-edge record and incomplete gene-by-gene tailoring validation preclude treating the 14-kb display as a proven self-sufficient complete pathway.
The defining fusion protein contains a sesquiterpene synthase (STS) domain and HMG-CoA synthase (HMGS) domain. Full-length and truncated STS constructs produce hirsutene via 1,11 cyclization.

Neighboring P450/oxidase genes provide plausible tailoring capacity, but their individual contributions to hirsutene-derived products are not treated as directly established by the defining hirsutene study.
Native expression context was studied in S. hirsutum cultures; a specific environmental activation trigger for the locus was NR.
Recombinant full-length and truncated STS constructs demonstrated hirsutene formation; the HMGS domain was independently shown functional in vivo by yeast complementation.
Native ecological role of hirsutene itself is NR in the defining biosynthetic study.
Do not transfer later hirsutene-tailoring assignments from other fungal species as direct S. hirsutum evidence.
ImqK is a cluster regulator used to activate the cryptic programme; imq-dependent chemistry yields tripeptide-derived imizoquin alkaloids assembled from an NRPS pathway.

Gene-by-gene enzyme assignments for all six products in the current MIBiG product list are not equally resolved; TMC-2A/B are retained as database-associated products without inventing step-specific causality.
Ralstonia solanacearum ralstonins suppress A. flavus germination and downregulate the imq cluster; forced ImqK activation exposes imizoquin production.

Regulator manipulation, metabolomics and supplementation experiments show that purified imizoquins rescue germination defects and protect against reactive oxygen stress; imizoquins also inhibit Ralstonia growth.
Imizoquins function in oxidative-stress protection during fungal germination and participate in chemical antagonism with Ralstonia.
Do not equate every compound listed in MIBiG with equally deep mechanistic resolution; the primary study most strongly resolves the imizoquin arm of the programme.
IacE is a prenyltransferase: ΔiacE abolishes iso-A82775C, accumulates prenyl-lacking siccayne, and redirects chemistry to new chloropestolides.
Later genetic/transcriptomic work identifies iacC, iacE, iacF, iacG, iacH and iacI as essential for iso-A82775C synthesis and places the cluster under CsdA/RsdA transcriptional control.

PfZipA affects iso-A82775C under oxidative-stress treatments, but this is encoded as global stress regulation rather than a pathway-specific switch. CsdA/RsdA provide stronger direct cluster-regulatory evidence.

ΔiacE genetics and metabolite profiling establish prenylation causality. New chloropestolides 5/6 showed antibacterial activity against S. aureus and B. subtilis; compound 5 was cytotoxic to HeLa, MCF-7 and SW480 cells.
Native ecological role of iso-A82775C remains UNCERTAIN; chemically it is a proposed precursor in chloropupukeananin/chloropestolide biosynthesis.
Global stress regulators are not equated with pathway-specific activation, and current MIBiG completeness remains unknown despite expanded iac-gene causality.

Current MIBiG genes in the S. chlorohalonata record are largely hypothetical; antiSMASH detects NRPS-like and type-I PKS signatures. Direct product-gene causality in the record strain was NF in the examined defining literature.

A proposed Stachybotrys isoindolinone model invokes a phthalic-dialdehyde precursor reacting spontaneously with ammonium or amino compounds, but this was studied in S. longispora FG216 and is not transferred as direct S. chlorohalonata evidence.
In S. longispora FG216, feeding amino compounds generated new isoindolinone derivatives. For S. chlorohalonata IBT 40285 specifically, an experimentally validated activation condition is NF.
Record-strain knockout, heterologous-expression or direct feeding validation was NF. The comparative S. longispora study fed amino compounds and isolated four new derivatives FGFC4–FGFC7.
Native ecological role and record-strain bioactivity are NR. FGFC6/FGFC7 fibrinolytic activity belongs to S. longispora-derived congeners and is not assigned to BGC0001626.

Species/strain mismatch is material: the defining feeding study is S. longispora FG216, whereas BGC0001626 is S. chlorohalonata IBT 40285. The database association is retained without upgrading comparative evidence to direct causality.
